overview: The New Kingdom followed Ahmose’s reunification of Egypt. The Met dates this Egyptian historical phase approximately 1550-1070 BCE, encompassing multiple dynasties and changing political centers.

items.text: Thebes remained a major religious and cultural center even when Dynasty 19 rulers based their administration in the Delta.
Successive rulers enlarged Karnak. Kings and courtiers dedicated statues in its temple precincts.
Rock-cut royal tombs carried painted and carved religious scenes concerning the afterlife.
Records from the artisans’ settlement at Deir el-Medina illuminate the community that made royal tombs.
The phase label spans changing administrations and artistic traditions. Its approximate endpoint should not become a claim that Egyptian civilization disappeared.

sources.title: Catharine Roehrig, Met, Egypt in the New Kingdom
